xyzopt.py

This page contains a Python script to optimize the molecular geometry and save the XYZ coordinates of the molecule in .xyz format.

Note

This script requires geomeTRIC Python library to update the nuclear coordinates in translation-rotation internal coordinates (TRIC) until the convergence criteria for energy change, gradient and atomic displacement successive steps all fall below prescribed convergence threshold (small enough).

#!/usr/bin/env python
# coding: utf-8
# edit by materials@dindagustiayu.com

# import directories
from pyscf import gto, scf
from pyscf.geomopt.geometric_solver import optimize

# Create the pyscf molecule
mol = gto.M(atom="mol.xyz")

mol.basis = "------"

# set the functional
mf = mol.KS()
mf.xc = '-----'

# Run optimization calculations
conv_params = {
'convergence_energy': 1e-6, # Eh
    'convergence_grms': 3e-4,   # Eh/Bohr
    'convergence_gmax': 4.5e-4, # Eh/Bohr
    'convergence_drms': 1.2e-3, # Angstrom
    'convergence_dmax': 1.8e-3, # Angstrom
}

mol_eq = optimize(mf, **conv_params)

# save the optimized geometry in XYZ format
mol_eq.tofile("opt_mol.xyz")
